cohort: 169 primiparous women (128 vaginal delivery, 41 cesarean delivery) followed up at 2 and 6 months postpartum
finding: Mode of delivery did not influence pelvic floor dysfunction, except for anal incontinence, and there was improvement in all outcomes over the study period.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery did not influence pelvic floor dysfunction, except for anal incontinence, where there was a significant interaction between mode of delivery and time.
